HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE AMIT MAHAJAN  ORDER % 14.08.2024 CRL.M.A. 24168/2024 (exemption from filing certified copy of the annexure).
1. Exemptions allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. The application stands disposed of.
The present petition is filed seeking quashing of the chargesheet arising out of FIR No. 76/2020 under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
4. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that false FIR has been filed to unnecessarily implicate the petitioners.
He submits that Petitioner No. 1 is the husband of the complainant and Petitioner Nos. 2 & 3 are the parents in law.
He submits that it is an admitted case that at least since the year 2014, the parties are not residing together.
He submits that, in fact, Petitioner This is a digitally signed order.

He submits that multiple proceedings have been initiated by the complainant under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC) as well as the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, which have been pending since the year Navdeep Gupta And Ors vs State Govt. 5.

sentences.text: He further submits that the parties were also referred to Mediation.
However, no settlement was arrived at.

He further vehemently contends that false affidavits were also filed by the complainant in various Courts which also led to filing of an application under Section 340 of the CrPC, which is pending consideration.

6. He further submits that the present FIR was registered belatedly in the year 2020 and the police has filed the chargesheet solely on the basis of the allegations made at the time of registration of the FIR.

He, however, at the outset, submits that since the matter is now listed for arguments on charge,
he will take all arguments before the learned Trial Court.
He, however, prays that Petitioner Nos. 2 & 3 being Senior Citizens be exempted from appearance before the learned Trial Court.
7. Considering the above, since the matter is now listed for arguments on charge, this Court does not consider it apposite to entertain this petition at this stage.
8. The petitioner is at liberty to take all arguments before the learned Trial Court, which would pass an order after considering the record and the arguments advanced by the parties.
The petitioners are also at liberty to file an appropriate application seeking exemption.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 20/08/2024 at 01:56:14 9.
Considering the age of Petitioner Nos. 2 & 3, the learned Trial Court is expected to take a lenient view as and when any application seeking exemption is filed.
10. The present petition is, therefore, dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to the petitioners to approach this Court in case any grievance remains in future.
11. The petitions are disposed of in the aforesaid terms.
AMIT MAHAJAN, J AUGUST 14, 2024 "SK"
